newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA reprimands former Barings executive.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA reprimands former Barings executive.

text.p: Britain's securities market watchdog, the Securiuties and Futures Authority, said on Friday it has reprimanded Mary Waltz, a former executive of investment bank Baring Brothers.

The SFA said Waltz, who will also pay 5,000 pounds towards the SFA's costs, has accepted that she "failed to act with due skill, care and dilligence in breach of the SFA's principles in that she did not properly monitor the bank's switching business undertaken by Singapore trader Nick Leeson which led to the collapse of the bank.
Waltz, head of equity derivatives in the Financial Products group run by Ron Baker who has also been reprimanded by the SFA. Baker announced recently that he will appeal the findings of the tribunal.

Leeson's unauthorised and undiscovered trading activities led to losses of around $1.4 billion and led to the collapse of the bank in February 1995 and its eventual purchase by Dutch financial group Internationale Nederlanden Groep.
Waltz recently lost an Industrial Tribunal claim for 500,000 pounds ($845,000) from ING Barings relating to bonus payments which she said were due to her.

The SFA now has two outstanding cases against former Barings personnel and has already banned several former executives from working in the financial markets including Peter Norris, former chief executive of the investment bank. ($1=.5922 Pound)
